title: Pruning, Defoliation and Training Response Limits

content.overview: Training practices redistribute growth, light exposure and labor rather than producing a guaranteed yield response. Plant response depends on genotype, timing, severity, environment and the objective being optimized.

vocabulary.definition: Intentional removal of leaves to alter canopy structure or exposure.
Removal of shoots, branches or growth points to alter plant architecture.
Relationship between tissues that produce/export assimilates and tissues that use/store them.

sections.title: Training changes architecture and resource distribution
sections.body: Pruning and branch manipulation can change where growth occurs and how light penetrates the canopy, but response depends on remaining leaf area and developmental timing.

sections.title: Cultivar response can differ
sections.body: A 2025 study found defoliation response differed between tested cannabis cultivars while spectral treatments also changed architecture. This argues against universal removal percentages.

sections.title: Define the production objective
sections.body: Training for height control, airflow, light uniformity or flower-size distribution may imply different choices. Measure the outcome rather than assuming a named technique succeeded.

workedExamples: A defoliation intensity that improves one cultivar's cannabinoid yield may provide no benefit or impose cost in another cultivar.
Removing lower growth can simplify canopy management but should be judged against labor, plant response and intended quality distribution.
commonMistakes: Using the same pruning intensity for every cultivar.
Removing foliage by a fixed percentage without measuring recovery.
Calling a technique successful because the canopy looks cleaner.
content.practicalApplication: For a training change, record cultivar, stage, tissue removed/manipulated, labor, light distribution and later growth/yield/quality response before standardizing it.
content.summary: Advanced training is an experiment with architecture and resource allocation, not a guaranteed recipe.
